title: The Provision of Mount Kessler
premise: Zephyrine Marchetti, a bush pilot who has spent seven years outrunning a wrongful conviction she never committed, accepts a dying prospector's map in exchange for a promise to deliver his findings to a daughter he abandoned. The map leads up the Kessler River to a source the mining syndicate has sealed off, where the truth about the crime Zephyrine was framed for is buried in an abandoned survey camp. Racing the brief window before glacier calving closes the route, she gathers an unlikely crew of river runners and outcasts who become the family she never let herself want. In the end she exposes the syndicate's fraud, clears her name, and chooses to stay in the interior, founding a flying service that carries medicine, justice, and belonging to those the law forgot.
about_author: Mirabel Coldharbour is the pen name of a former floatplane mechanic who spent a decade in remote northern camps before turning to writing full-time. She is known for adventure novels that pair white-knuckle wilderness sequences with quietly fierce meditations on the families people build when the world has written them off.

chapters.title: Fuel and Rumors
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A routine medicine run into the interior establishes her life measured in miles: precise, solitary, unattached. She overhears rumors that a survey team is asking about a pilot named Marchetti. The emotional beat is the practiced ease of avoidance, and the first hairline crack in it.

chapters.title: The Dying Prospector
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She lands at a remote cabin to find old Tobias Wrenn injured and dying. He trades her a hand-drawn map of the Kessler headwaters for a promise: deliver his packet to a daughter in Coldbank. The beat is a bargain struck between two people who understand what it costs to disappear.

chapters.title: Coldbank
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with a brief interlude from the daughter, Ruth Wrenn, a hard-edged ferry operator. Ruth refuses the packet and her father's name. Zephyrine glimpses the map's markings and recognizes the sealed survey camp where she was framed seven years ago. Beat: the past stops being somewhere else.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Alone in her hangar, she deciphers Wrenn's notations: ore samples, dates, and a ledger page proving the syndicate falsified the survey that incriminated her. The calving season gives her perhaps three weeks. Beat: fear transmuting into resolve; she decides to go upstream.

chapters.title: The River Runner
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Zephyrine comes to ask about running the Kessler gorge. Ruth refuses, then relents when she reads her father's letter, furious and grieving at once. Beat: two guarded women discovering they are more alike than either will admit.

chapters.title: Assembling the Crew
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She recruits Dez, a disgraced geologist who can read rock, and Junie, a teenage runaway mechanic who stows away aboard and refuses to be left behind. Beat: the reluctant first stitching of a found family, each member pretending it's temporary.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The expedition launches by boat and floatplane shuttle. The river narrows, the syndicate's patrol boat shadows them, and Dez confirms the ore samples could only have come from the forbidden source. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by the sense of being hunted.

chapters.title: Patrol at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The syndicate boat boards them under a pretext; Zephyrine talks her way through with a forged permit, but the inspector photographs everyone. Junie, who trusts no adults, notices Zephyrine lying to protect her. Beat: the first flicker of trust.

chapters.title: The Portage
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. A grueling two-day portage around an unrunnable gorge tests the crew; Dez's old injury flares, and Ruth carries the load he cannot. Around the fire, Ruth tells Zephyrine about the night her father left. Beat: grief shared is weight halved.

chapters.title: Ice on the Wind
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Signs of early calving appear; the window is shrinking faster than forecast. A syndicate floatplane strafes their camp with warnings, and Zephyrine realizes they know exactly who she is. Beat: the stakes sharpen from discovery to survival.

chapters.title: Dez's Confession
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. He admits he signed the falsified survey report under threat, and has spent seven years drinking himself numb. Zephyrine chooses not to turn him away. Beat: the theme of justice outside the law takes shape; the crew becomes its own tribunal and absolution.

chapters.title: The Tributary Trap
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The syndicate sabotages their boat at a tributary junction. Junie's mechanical skill saves the engine, but they lose two days and half their fuel. Beat: competence under pressure, and Junie's slow conversion from stowaway to indispensable crew.

chapters.title: The Hermit of Kessler Bend
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. They shelter with a hermit trapper who once flew with Zephyrine's father, and who reveals her father died searching for evidence to clear her name. Beat: Zephyrine learns her exile was witnessed and mourned; belonging reaches backward through time.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A freak storm forces a blind landing on a glacial lake; the plane is damaged, stranding them with the source two days' hike away. Beat: despair at the edge of the window, and the choice to go on foot rather than turn back.

chapters.title: The Sealed Camp
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. They reach the abandoned survey camp and find Wrenn's hidden cache: the original ore ledger, correspondence, and proof the syndicate manufactured the evidence against her. Beat: vindication that feels strangely hollow until Ruth's hand on her shoulder makes it real.

chapters.title: The Syndicate Arrives
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. The syndicate's enforcer, Voss, and his men surround the camp, having tracked them since the Narrows. Voss offers Zephyrine her old life back if she burns the ledger. Beat: the temptation of the legal justice she was denied, weighed against the people standing beside her.

chapters.title: The Calving
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The glacier calves early, and the icefall avalanche traps Voss's men and splits the camp. In the chaos, Zephyrine goes back into the collapse zone to pull Voss out. Beat: the climax of character; she saves the man who came to destroy her, choosing who she is over who she was made to be.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. With Voss a battered, disarmed prisoner of his own men's abandonment, the crew runs the river down through the opened ice corridor, the only window they will ever get. Beat: pure adventure catharsis, the found family functioning as one body.

chapters.title: Coldbank Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. They deliver the ledger to a magistrate outside syndicate reach, and Voss, facing his own employers' reprisal, corroborates everything. The conviction is voided. Beat: justice arrives, but the chapter's warmth comes from the crew realizing they no longer need it to stay together.

chapters.title: The Daughter's Letter
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Ruth finally reads her father's letter in full and finds he named her in his mining claim, giving her the source itself. Ruth asks Zephyrine to fly the claim's supply runs. Beat: inheritance redefined; the river belongs to the people who carried each other up it.

chapters.title: Grounded on Purpose
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The crew rebuilds the damaged plane together at Kessler Bend. Zephyrine formally offers Junie an apprenticeship and a room, and for the first time in seven years Zephyrine signs a lease instead of a fuel chit. Beat: the quiet climax of belonging; staying as a deliberate act of courage.

chapters.title: The Provision of Mount Kessler
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, closing. A year later, the Marchetti-Wrenn Air Service flies medicine, mail, and second chances into the interior. On the anniversary of the calving, the crew scatters Wrenn's ashes at the source. Final beat: life no longer measured in miles, but in the people waiting at the end of each flight.
